data.label: Capture New Lead
data.rationale: This is a deterministic event trigger from a form submission. It can be handled with simple webhook or form event routing at L0; no ML, NLP, or LLM behavior is needed.
conditions: Required fields present: email, name, company
data.description: Trigger when a new lead is submitted through the website form.
data.errorHandling: If payload is missing required fields, reject the event with a 400 response and log the validation failure. If the webhook times out or duplicates the event, deduplicate using an idempotency key and retry delivery once.

data.label: Validate Email Format
data.rationale: Email format validation is pure rule-based logic using regex or standard validation libraries. L0 is sufficient and preferred because the outcome is fully deterministic.
data.description: Check whether the submitted email address follows a valid format.
data.errorHandling: If email validation fails, stop the workflow and mark the lead as invalid. Return a structured error reason for the CRM record or form intake log. No retry is needed because the failure is data-related.

data.label: Check CRM Duplicates
data.rationale: Duplicate checking is a deterministic CRM lookup and comparison task. It relies on exact or rule-based matching, so L0 is appropriate without needing ML or language understanding.
data.description: Search the CRM to determine whether the lead already exists as a duplicate.
data.errorHandling: If the CRM lookup fails, retry the read operation with exponential backoff up to 3 times. If still unavailable, queue the lead for later reconciliation and stop downstream actions to avoid duplicate creation.

data.label: Score Lead
data.rationale: Scoring can be implemented as deterministic business rules at L0, but the presence of multiple signals such as company size, industry, and engagement history often benefits from a trained predictive model. Since the workflow implies variable scoring based on historical patterns, L1 is the best fit. No language generation is required.
data.description: Assign a lead score using company size, industry, and engagement history.
data.errorHandling: If model scoring fails or required features are missing, fall back to a rule-based score using available attributes. If the model file is unavailable, use the fallback scoring function and flag the record for later model health review.

data.label: Evaluate Score Threshold
data.rationale: This is a straightforward threshold-based decision tree. It is fully deterministic conditional logic, so L0 is sufficient.
data.description: Branch the workflow based on the lead score range.
data.errorHandling: If score is null, NaN, or out of expected range, route the lead to manual review and log a scoring anomaly. Do not proceed to automated routing without a valid score.

data.label: Route to Sales Rep
data.rationale: Routing the lead to a rep is deterministic, but generating a personalized summary requires language generation. A single LLM call can draft the summary from available lead data, so L3 is sufficient. No external tool use is required for the generation itself.
data.description: Assign the lead to a sales representative and attach a personalized summary.
data.errorHandling: If summary generation fails, send the lead to sales with a templated fallback summary and retry the LLM call once. If rep assignment fails, place the lead in a sales queue and alert ops.

data.label: Add to Nurture Campaign
data.rationale: This is a deterministic CRM or marketing automation action based on the score threshold. No uncertainty handling, ML, or language understanding is needed.
data.description: Enroll the lead in the nurture campaign for lower-scoring prospects.
data.errorHandling: If the campaign API fails, retry the enrollment up to 3 times with backoff. If still unsuccessful, store the lead in a pending nurture queue and alert the marketing team.

data.label: Flag for Manual Review
data.rationale: Flagging a lead for human review and sending a notification is deterministic workflow logic. L0 is enough because the step does not require interpretation or generation beyond a standard message template.
data.description: Notify the sales team to review leads with mid-range scores.
data.errorHandling: If notification delivery fails, create a CRM task for manual review and retry the notification once. If both fail, persist the review request in a dead-letter queue.

data.label: Complete Lead Handling
data.rationale: Workflow completion is a pure terminal state with no decision-making or AI involvement. It is entirely deterministic at L0.
conditions: downstream action completed or safely queued
data.description: Mark the lead processing workflow as complete after the appropriate action is taken.
data.errorHandling: If final status persistence fails, retry the write once and then emit an operational alert. The workflow should remain idempotent so completion can be safely re-applied.

data.label: Human Review Gate
data.description: Manual approval checkpoint for mid-range scored leads before final disposition.
data.rationale: This governance checkpoint ensures ambiguous leads receive human oversight before automated follow-up decisions are finalized.
data.errorHandling: If a reviewer does not respond within the SLA, escalate the task to the team lead and keep the lead in a pending-review state.

message: Configured moderate governance for a customer-facing lead routing workflow. Logging is standard with step snapshots enabled. Thresholds are tightened to reflect customer-facing impact and the presence of an L3 sales-summary step, while keeping operational costs low. A human review gate was added for mid-range scores to enforce oversight before final disposition.

workflow.workflowBrief: When a new lead comes in through the website form, validate the email format and check for duplicates in the CRM. Score the lead based on company size, industry, and engagement history. If the score is above 80, route to a sales rep with a personalized summary. If below 40, add to the nurture campaign. For scores in between, flag for manual review by the sales team.
